Privacy Preference Center content: When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to find out more and change our default settings. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Strictly Necessary Cookies description: These cookies are necessary for the web application to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Targeting Cookies description: These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
Functional Cookies description: These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.
Performance Cookies description: These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our web application. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the web application. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our web application, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Search Options: General Search Options・AND Search (including multiple words [delimiter:blank] at the same time) ex.A B → A B,AB,AcB,…・OR  Search (including multiple words [delimiter:blank])        ex.A B → A,B,Ac,cB,A B,AB,AcB,…・Partial Match (with start digit) ex, 34 from dig.5: JP1234,112234 / 123 from dig.3: JP1234,001234・Exact Match ex.AB → AB only (×: aB, 0AB, ABAB,…)・Start with    ex.A → A,AB,AcB,A000,A12,A_0,… (×:aAB,0AB,_AB,…)・End with    ex.A → A,BA,BcA,000A,12A,0_A,… (×:aAB,B0A,A_B,…)Regular Expression: Specify the format, such as serial, in detail　\d{10} :10-digit number                 ex.1234567890,0987654321　7\d{9} :10-digit number starting with 7 ex.7123456789　\d{3,5}:3-5 digit number                ex.123,4567,89012,… (×:12,ABC,123456,…)　\w{5}  :5-digit alphabet/_/number[a-zA-Z_0-9](hereinafter referred to as letter)　\w{3}-\d{4} :3-digit letter + hyphen + 4-digit number                  ex.AB3-1234　JP\d{10}    :12-digit number starting with JP (DNJP part number, etc.) ex.JP1234567890　(JP|EN)\d{2}:4-digit character starting with JP or EN                  ex.JP12,EN34

Accuracy description:
Number of correct predictions made divided by the total number of data.
If the number of positive labels is extremely smaller than the negative labels (example: OK/NG data), consider using precision/recall/PR-AUC.
Precision description:
Higher value indicates the fewer false alarms (false positives).
Number of correct predictions made divided by the number of positive predictions.
Recall description:
Higher value indicates the fewer overlooks of the positive labels.
Number of correct predictions made divided by the number of positive labels.
ROC-AUC description:
Use when the number of positive/negative labels is balanced.
Higher value indicates the higher performance to both labels.
The area under the curve when plotting the relationship between the false positive rate and the true positive rate while changing the threshold.
PR-AUC description:
Use when the number of positive labels is extremely smaller than the negative labels.
Higher value indicates the higher performance of predicting the positive labels.
The area under the curve when plotting the relationship between the precision and the recall while changing the threshold.

Window length Hover:
Enter the time width for calculating one distribution. Please enter a number between 0.01 (=36 seconds) and less than 20,000 (=833 days). If it is equal to the step size, evaluate all data without overlap (recommended setting). If it is larger than the step size, data overlap will occur (effective when there is little data. However, since some of the same data is evaluated, there is a concern that changes may become slow). If the value is smaller than the step size, data will not overlap and some data will not be evaluated (effective when there is a large number of data. However, not recommended as some data will not be evaluated). 
e.g.) 1 week = 168h, 30 days = 720h, a half year = 4320h, one year = 8760h

   “ab|c” to search for items containing either “ab” or “c” (OR condition), and
   “^(?!test|abc).*” to find items starting something other than “test” or “abc”.
(“^” indicates that the next character is at the beginning, “$” indicates that the preceding character is at the end, and “|” means OR.
Note: The quotation marks are not needed when entering the values.)

Waveform Plot Description:
You can visualize waveforms for each cycle.
Multiple waveforms can be plotted on a single graph, and coloring is also supported.
For example, by comparing press‑fit waveforms, current waveforms,
or vibration waveforms of good and defective products,
you can identify rising‑edge changes in specific sections or detect variations in peak positions.
WfP Display variable hover:
Select two variables: the x‑value and y‑value of the waveforms. The first selected variable becomes the x‑axis.
Selecting a 'Div' variable (used to group identical waveforms, such as Cycle ID) is mandatory.

ImportLimitTitle:
Limits the number of rows to import.
The limit applies to each process (e.g., for a database: table, for CSV: folder).
If you decrease the limit or when importing the latest data, if the number of rows exceeds the limit,
the oldest data will be deleted from database in AP+DN7.
When the import limit is increased, the data previously imported into AP+DN7 is first deleted and then re-imported from the data sources.
